correctness.rationale: Finite normalization of a reduced projective curve factors through finite simple gluings and a finite bijection. Across any simple gluing, the geometric fiber over multiplicity m is m+1 points, with m correction points; MacPherson functoriality gives the exact integral formula even for disconnected sources. Disjoint-union external CSM products establish the smooth normalization base. Nil-invariance extends to nonreduced schemes. For genus-positive normalization, the smooth-curve canonical-zero factorization yields an exact polynomial of degree D with top term of degree ±1. Critical steps and all boundary cases are detailed in RESULT.md; no finite experiments are used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary source arXiv:2610.31826v1 was read in sections 1,4,5, especially its exact restrictive curve definition preceding Proposition 5.6. The source establishes integral equality for irreducible reduced complete curves, not arbitrary one-dimensional projective schemes or their branch-corrected sharp vanishing. The new argument generalizes the simple-gluing lemma to distinct connected components, then uses disjoint-union products and nil-invariance. Semantic mathematical-record comparisons and web literature searches found no equivalent covering theorem. Priority risk is substantial because the gluing mechanism is close to the original proof; this is an extension, not an unrelated discovery.
residual_risks: The reducible-case extension is conceptually close to source Proposition 5.11 and may be judged implicit in its argument; independent literature-priority review required.

value.rationale: The theorem completes a natural dimension-one class of an expressly stated integral Chow-valued Macdonald conjecture beyond the irreducible-curve case, and supplies an explicit normalization-branch product. It yields sharp integral cycle-class vanishing in all sufficiently large symmetric powers for reducible positive-genus curves, a stronger conclusion than the source's general modulo-factorial result and stronger than classical numerical Euler-series vanishing. For nodal unions of elliptic curves it provides an exact Chow-valued polynomial of prescribed arbitrary degree.
